title: Lesson 61 - Which One Makes More Sense?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: We have three feedback methods: a large-print paper checklist, a QR form, or a short facilitated debrief. Which one makes more sense for this rehearsal?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Before we choose, what are our criteria?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: No personal device should be required, comments should identify an exact location, and collection should finish within fifteen minutes.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: We also have only one facilitator. Compared with paper, the QR form is cheaper and faster to submit.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: That’s true, but it requires a phone and a stable connection. The paper checklist works without either.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The paper version costs eighteen dollars to print and takes about three minutes per tester. Its main advantage is that people can mark the route map directly.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The downside is later data entry. With the QR form, the results would already be organized by location.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The facilitated debrief could produce more detailed explanations, whereas a checklist might produce shorter answers.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It takes about five minutes per person, though. Three separate conversations would use the whole fifteen-minute collection window.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: And a group debrief would be quicker, but one person’s comments might influence the others.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: So the paper checklist meets the device and location criteria better than the QR form.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The QR form performs better on cost and data entry. Neither option is better on every criterion.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Exactly. Our top priority is collecting location-specific comments without requiring a personal device.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: That rules out using QR as the only method for this rehearsal.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What about the debrief? It gives richer detail than paper.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Yes, but it leaves no time margin. We need to allow time for instructions and one late tester.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Because the checklist meets the two highest-priority criteria, it makes more sense as the default.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Therefore, my recommendation is paper for the rehearsal, with one optional spoken follow-up question.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: On balance, that is the best available option for this thirty-minute session, not necessarily for the public event.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Agreed. Let’s confirm the printing cost and large-print layout before we treat the recommendation as final.
